title: Shortest Distance After Road Addition Queries II
summary: Given an integer n and a series of queries, each adding a unidirectional road between two cities.
statement: Given an integer n and a series of queries, each adding a unidirectional road between two cities. After each query, determine the shortest path length from city 0 to city n-1. Return an array of these shortest path lengths after each query, with no two queries violating the specified order condition.
constraints: 3≤n≤100,000 and the initial directed chain contains i→i+1.
Every query adds a forward shortcut, and no two shortcut intervals cross.
Return the current shortest 0-to-(n-1) edge count after every query.
hints: Noncrossing shortcuts let the current shortest route be represented as one forward linked chain.
When a useful shortcut arrives, splice out every active chain node strictly inside its interval.
Each removed link reduces the route length once; mark removed nodes with zero so they are never processed again.
Laminar intervals ensure a discarded chain segment can never be needed later, giving amortized linear splicing.
editorial: Laminar intervals ensure a discarded chain segment can never be needed later, giving amortized linear splicing.

tests.explanation: The maintained route lengths become three, two, then one.
Once the direct edge exists, the distance remains one.
